items.statement: Use Water for Injection for parenteral products where pyrogens are a concern, both to formulate the product and for the final washing of components and equipment used to make it.
items.quote: For parenteral products where there is a concern for pyrogens, it is expected that Water for Injection will be used. This applies to the formulation of products, as well as to the final washing of components and equipment used in their manufacture.
items.condition: parenteral products where pyrogens are a concern

items.statement: Formulate ophthalmic and inhalation products that have pyrogen specifications (for example ophthalmic irrigating solution or Sterile Water for Inhalation) with Water for Injection.
items.quote: For some ophthalmic products, such as the ophthalmic irrigating solution, and some inhalation products, such as Sterile Water for Inhalation, where there are pyrogen specifications, it is expected that Water for Injection be used in their formulation.
items.condition: ophthalmic or inhalation products with pyrogen specifications

items.statement: Set more stringent microbial limits for water used in products whose preservatives are only marginally effective, such as antacids.
items.quote: For example, preservatives in antacids are marginally effective, so more stringent microbial limits have to be set.

items.statement: Have quality control assess every product made with the system's water and set the water's microbial action limits based on the product most sensitive to microbes.
items.quote: The quality control department should assess each product manufactured with the water from their system and determine the microbial action limits based on the most microbial sensitive product.

items.statement: Instead of setting stringent water action limits for the system, a microbial reduction step may be added to the manufacturing process of the sensitive drug product(s).
items.quote: In lieu of stringent water action limits in the system the manufacturer can add a microbial reduction step in the manufacturing process for the sensitive drug product(s).
items.condition: instead of stringent water action limits

items.statement: When validating a water system, do not challenge the on-line system with microorganisms; instead rely on periodic microbiological testing and monitoring equipment installed at specific checkpoints to show the whole system works properly and continuously.
items.quote: it would be undesirable to introduce microorganisms into an on-line system; therefore, reliance is placed on periodic testing for microbiological quality and on the installation of monitoring equipment at specific checkpoints to ensure that the total system is operating properly and continuously fulfilling its intended function.

items.statement: Include in the water system documentation a description of the system together with a drawing (print).
items.quote: Documentation should include a description of the system along with a print.

items.statement: Make the water system drawing show all equipment from the water feed to the points of use, and all sampling points with their designations.
items.quote: The drawing needs to show all equipment in the system from the water feed to points of use. It should also show all sampling points and their designations.

items.statement: Compare the system drawing against the actual water system every year to ensure it is accurate, to detect unreported changes and to confirm reported changes.
items.quote: The print should be compared to the actual system annually to insure its accuracy, to detect unreported changes and confirm reported changes to the system.

items.statement: Start the initial phase of water system validation only after all equipment and piping has been verified as correctly installed and working as specified, and use this phase to develop the operating parameters and the cleaning/sanitization procedures and frequencies.
items.quote: After all the equipment and piping has been verified as installed correctly and working as specified, the initial phase of the water system validation can begin. During this phase the operational parameters and the cleaning/ sanitization procedures and frequencies will be developed.

items.statement: During the initial validation phase, sample daily after each purification step and at each point of use for two to four weeks.
items.quote: Sampling should be daily after each step in the purification process and at each point of use for two to four weeks.

items.statement: Draw point-of-use samples the same way the water is drawn for use, e.g. at the end of the hose if a hose is usually attached, and after flushing if the procedure requires flushing before use.
items.quote: The sampling procedure for point of use sampling should reflect how the water is to be drawn e.g. if a hose is usually attached the sample should be taken at the end of the hose. If the SOP calls for the line to be flushed before use of the water from that point, then the sample is taken after the flush.

items.statement: Have the standard operating procedures for running the water system developed by the end of the two-to-four-week initial phase.
items.quote: At the end of the two to four week time period the firm should have developed its SOPs for operation of the water system.

items.statement: In a second validation phase, sample as in the initial phase and for the same period, and show with the data that the system consistently produces water of the desired quality when operated according to its procedures.
items.quote: The second phase of the system validation is to demonstrate that the system will consistently produce the desired water quality when operated in conformance with the SOPs. The sampling is performed as in the initial phase and for the same time period. At the end of this phase the data should demonstrate that the system will consistently produce the desired quality of water.

items.statement: In a third validation phase, sample according to routine procedures and frequencies to show that the system, operated per its procedures over a long period, consistently produces water of the desired quality, capturing feedwater quality variations that could affect it.
items.quote: The third phase of validation is designed to demonstrate that when the water system is operated in accordance with the SOPs over a long period of time it will consistently produce water of the desired quality. Any variations in the quality of the feedwater that could affect the operation and ultimately the water quality will be picked up during this phase of the validation. Sampling is performed according to routine procedures and frequencies.

items.statement: For Water for Injection systems during the long-term validation phase, sample at least one point of use daily and test all points of use weekly.
items.quote: For Water for Injection systems the samples should be taken daily from a minimum of one point of use, with all points of use tested weekly.

items.statement: Do not consider water system validation complete until a full year of data has been collected.
items.quote: The validation of the water system is completed when the firm has a full years worth of data.

items.statement: Have data that support the water system operating procedures.
items.quote: First, there must be data to support the SOPs.

items.statement: Have data showing that the operating procedures are valid and that the system can consistently produce water meeting the desired specifications.
items.quote: Second, there must be data demonstrating that the SOPs are valid and that the system is capable of consistently producing water that meets the desired specifications.

items.statement: Have data showing that seasonal feedwater variations do not adversely affect system operation or water quality.
items.quote: Finally, there must be data to demonstrate that seasonal variations in the feedwater do not adversely affect the operation of the system or the water quality.

items.statement: Compile the validation data and any conclusions into a final validation report.
items.quote: The last part of the validation is the compilation of the data, with any conclusions into the final report.

items.statement: Have the final water system validation report signed by the appropriate people responsible for operating the system and for its quality assurance.
items.quote: The final validation report must be signed by the appropriate people responsible for operation and quality assurance of the water system.

items.statement: Write operating procedures requiring the secondary valve to be opened before the primary valve so the drained pipe is flushed before use, preventing non-sterile air contaminating the system.
items.quote: The solution is to pro-vide for operational procedures that provide for opening the secondary valve before the primary valve to flush the pipe prior to use.

items.statement: Base the water system validation acceptance criteria primarily on consistent results throughout the system over a period of time.
items.quote: Another major consideration in the validation of high purity water systems is the acceptance criteria. Consistent results throughout the system over a period of time constitute the primary element.

items.statement: Water for Injection microbiological results should be essentially sterile.
items.quote: Regarding microbiological results, for Water For Injection, it is expected that they be essentially sterile.

items.statement: An action limit of less than 10 CFU/100 mL is acceptable for Water for Injection.
items.quote: Agency policy, is that less than 10 CFU/100ml is an acceptable action limit.

items.statement: Treat all water limits as action limits, not as pass/fail limits.
items.quote: None of the limits for water are pass/fail limits. All limits are action limits.

items.statement: When a water action limit is exceeded, investigate the cause, correct the problem, assess the impact of the microbial contamination on products made with the water, and document the investigation results.
items.quote: When action limits are exceeded the firm must investigate the cause of the problem, take action to correct the problem and assess the impact of the microbial contamination on products manufactured with the water and document the results of their investigation.

items.statement: When sampling Water for Injection systems, use a sample volume of preferably 100 to 300 mL and never less than 100 mL.
items.quote: With regard to sample size, 100 - 300 mL is preferred when sampling Water for Injection systems. Sample volumes less than 100 mL are unacceptable.

items.statement: Monitor Water for Injection systems for both endotoxins and microorganisms.
items.quote: Because WFI can pass the LAL endotoxin test and still fail the above microbial action limit, it is important to monitor WFI systems for both endotoxins and microorganisms.

items.statement: As a minimum, purified water should comply with the federal EPA regulations for drinking water.
items.quote: USP XXII specifications, that it complies with federal Environmental Protection Agency regulations for drinking water, are recognized as being minimal specifications.

items.statement: Set the action limit for a purified water system at no more than 100 CFU/mL.
items.quote: Agency policy is that any action limit over 100 CFU/mL for a purified water system is unacceptable.

items.statement: Base each purified water action limit on the overall purified water system, the further processing of the finished product and the product's use.
items.quote: Any action limit established will depend upon the overall purified water system and further processing of the finished product and its use.

items.statement: Ensure purified water used to make drug products by cold processing is free of objectionable organisms.
items.quote: For example, purified water used to manufacture drug products by cold processing should be free of objectionable organisms.
items.condition: drug products made by cold processing

items.statement: When setting the contamination level allowed in a high purity water system used for a non-sterile product, take into account the product's use, its formulation (preservative system) and its manufacturing process.
items.quote: Thus, in establishing the level of contamination allowed in a high purity water system used in the manufacture of a non-sterile product requires an understanding of the use of the product, the formulation (preservative system) and manufacturing process.

items.statement: For products without an effective preservative system, such as antacids, set the water action limit below the 100 CFU/mL maximum.
items.quote: For example, antacids, which do not have an effective preservative system, require an action limit below the 100 CFU/mL maximum.
items.condition: products without an effective preservative system

items.statement: Evaluate the products and how they are made, and set an acceptable water system action level, not above the maximum, based on the highest-risk product made with the water.
items.quote: It is up to each manufacturer to evaluate their product, the way it is manufactured, and establish am acceptable action level of contamination, not to exceed the maximum, for the water system, based on the highest risk product manufactured with the water.

items.statement: Pretreat feedwater for reverse osmosis units, and for distillation equipment as most still manufacturers recommend.
items.quote: Pretreatment of feedwater is recommended by most manufacturers of distillation equipment and is definitely required for RO units.

items.statement: Design the water system to operate within the anticipated extremes of feedwater quality, such as seasonal and other external variations.
items.quote: A water system should be designed to operate within these anticipated extremes.

items.statement: Monitor the feedwater periodically to know its quality extremes.
items.quote: Obviously, the only way to know the extremes is to periodically monitor feedwater.

items.statement: Where feedwater comes from a municipal water system, the municipality's test reports may be used instead of in-house testing.
items.quote: If the feedwater is from a municipal water system, reports from the municipality testing can be used in lieu of in-house testing.

items.statement: Have a satisfactory feedwater pretreatment system for stills so that the water system can be shown to be validated.
items.quote: Unless a firm has a satisfactory pretreatment system, it would be extremely difficult for them to demonstrate that the system is validated.

items.statement: Where distillation units producing WFI show maintenance or operating problems, be able to show from the system design, system changes, the validation report and routine test data that the system operates in a state of control.
items.quote: If you see these types of problems you should look very closely at the system design, any changes that have been made to the system, the validation report and the routine test data to determine if the system is operating in a state of control.

items.statement: Provide petcocks or small sampling ports between each piece of equipment (for example after the still and before the holding tank) so major equipment can be isolated for qualification and for investigating problems.
items.quote: Figures 3-5 also show petcocks or small sampling ports between each piece of equipment, such as after the still and before the holding tank. These are in the system to isolate major pieces of equipment. This is necessary for the qualification of the equipment and for the investigation of any problems which might occur.

items.statement: Use positive pressure, for example vapor compression or a double tubesheet design, to prevent feedwater contaminating the distillate through a leaking heat exchanger.
items.quote: Positive pressure such as in vapor compression or double tubesheet design should be employed to prevent possible feedwater to distillate contamination in a leaky heat exchanger.

items.statement: Prevent contamination by heat exchanger leakage either with gauges that constantly monitor pressure differentials so the clean fluid side is always at the higher pressure, or with a double-tubesheet heat exchanger.
items.quote: The guide points out that there are two methods for preventing contamination by leakage. One is to provide gauges to constantly monitor pressure differentials to ensure that the higher pressure is always on the clean fluid side. The other is to utilize the double-tubesheet type of heat exchanger.

items.statement: Do not drain the cooling water from use-point heat exchangers when they are not in use.
items.quote: Thus, it is recommended that when not in use, heat exchangers not be drained of the cooling water.

items.statement: Have a program for integrity testing the holding tank vent filter to make sure it is intact.
items.quote: It is expected that there be some program for integrity testing this filter to assure that it is intact.

items.statement: Place the holding tank vent filter where it is readily accessible.
items.quote: It is expected, therefore, that the vent filter be located in a position on the holding tank where it is readily accessible.
